appraisal_events.evidence: The duchesse first defends her — « C’est au contraire une excellente créature qui n’a jamais dit du mal de personne, ni fait de mal à personne » — then, when the princesse suggests malice often accompanies wit, adds « Ah ! cela par exemple elle en a encore moins », leaving Mme de Parme « stupéfaite » : « Moins d’esprit ?… »
appraisal_events.explanation: Under the cover of clearing her cousin of the charge of médisance, the duchesse delivers a far more damaging verdict in the salon's own currency: the woman has even less wit than malice. The ostensible praise ("excellente créature") is the setup for the sting, so the passage stages the defense ironically rather than endorsing it.

status_effects.explanation: She is cleared of malice only to be declared nearly devoid of esprit, which demolishes the "intelligence supérieure" the princesse had just credited her with; in this milieu wit is the decisive measure, so the net local movement is sharply downward.
The duchesse controls the whole exchange, converting a conventional defense into a lethal mot and holding the floor as the arbiter of who has wit.

Despite her superior rank, the princesse is twice wrong-footed by the same speech act: corrected about the rumor of médisance, briefly "soulagée", then left "stupéfaite" and reduced to asking for confirmation of a joke she did not see coming.

ambiguities: The target of the whole exchange is never named in the passage itself (only "elle" / "la"); she is identified as "votre cousine d’Heudicourt" in the immediately preceding window and does not appear on the reference sheet, so she is recorded under that surface form as unresolved.
